1edcblp:562: The core value of the Claude Code architecture lies in transforming "wild functions" into "controlled objects with full runtime semantics", which means the tool layer is not simply exposing function calls, but a complete runtime that includes execution context, permission checks, and state management.^(raw/articles/claude-code-architecture-analysis) Six major modules form a layered architecture: the entry chain handles process initialization and state separation; the REPL serves as a runtime console and maintains continuous interaction with the user; the Query Loop drives continuous execution in a state-machine pattern, supporting Compact compression and recovery; the Tool Runtime is the convergence point for cross-cutting complexity; the Permission System provides a complete decision chain rather than mere pop-ups; the Task abstraction provides a unified task-reclaim mechanism for multi-agent.^(raw/articles/claude-code-architecture-analysis) The most noteworthy design principle of this architecture is "external dynamism, internal convergence" — MCP/Skills/Plugins can be dynamically extended, but internal module boundaries are clear and dependency relationships are stable. This directly answers why many Agent systems are strong at the demo stage but begin to "deform" once the number of tools grows: they lack a runtime architecture that truly absorbs complexity.^(raw/articles/claude-code-architecture-analysis)
